utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll have that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, in your statement, you said that the Yugoslav People's Army in Bosnia-Herzegovina took away the weapons of the Territorial Defence. You said sometime in the beginning of 1990, if I read this right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You put it that way: Taken away. Was -- these weapons that were taken away from the warehouses of the TO, wasn't that done on the basis of the decision of the presidency on the 29th of April, 1990?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was probably some kind of a decision on the basis of which this was taken away; however, it was taken away, and the reasons are well known.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But there was a decision of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I imagine that there were legal grounds for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Presidency was the collective head of state of the SFRY; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It consisted of eight members; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, eight members.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Republic, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had its representative there; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you something else in reference to a certain fact. Do you know that the Presidency of the SFRY, on the 9th of January, 1991, passed an order to disband all armed units that were not within the armed forces of the SFRY and organs of the Ministry of the Interior? Are you aware of that decision, or rather, that order issued by the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Probably something like that was adopted, but I can't remember exactly. Perhaps in relation to the events in Croatia, as far as I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One more document that I would like to show to this witness, and it is just one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead. And before I forget, on the documents, you still have the obligation to get it from the Internet and hand it over to the Trial Chamber, because next time counsel may be tempted to say, "Oh, the Trial Chamber can offer the documents on the Internet." These are documents for your case, so you have the obligation to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D13/4 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, is this the Official Gazette of the SFRY, number 75, dated the 18th of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please, could you read sentence 765 only.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the basis of Article 316, paragraph 1, of the Constitution of the SFRY, and Article 6 of the law on All People's Defence, the Official Gazette of the SFRY number 21/82 and 35/91, the Presidency of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia has, at the session held on the 1st of October, 1991, when assessing the current political security situation in the country, ascertained the existence of an immediate threat of war in the SFRY. This enactment shall be published in the Official Gazette of the SFRY."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. Can we see from that that the Presidency of the SFRY ascertained that there was an immediate threat of war in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tihic, I would now like us to move on to another subject. Can we agree that the then Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was divided into military districts?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Part of Bosnia-Herzegovina and part of Croatia, up to the Hungarian border, was that the 2nd Military District?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was the command of the 2nd Military District in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Within this 2nd Military District, was there the 17th Tuzla Corps of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the Tuzla Corps. I don't know whether it was the 17th or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This 17th Tuzla Corps, did it form the 17th Tactical Group, with its headquarters in Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next question, of course, would be whether the order of the commander of the 17th Tactical Group established, inter alia, the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was precisely through that order. However, we thought that that was illegal, because this is a form of territorial defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have already presented your point of view while giving testimony. On the basis of all of this that we just agreed upon, can we also agree that the 4th Detachment was a unit of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military hierarchy, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that, within this 17th Tactical Group, there were four detachments?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, since this was the 4th one, there were probably a 1st, 2nd and 3rd one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now we are interested in the composition of these detachments. Can we agree that they were established by the local population that had been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Specifically, I'm referring to the 4th Detachment now. Can we agree that it was established in public?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While giving evidence before this Trial Chamber, you mentioned that Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... this point that the 4th Detachment was established in public. Maybe it's the interpretation. I don't seem to understand what that means. Maybe you can ask the witness, because he said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, through my next question, I was trying to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before this Tribunal, Mr. Tihic, in your statement, you mentioned that Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, at a meeting in the Samac municipality, gave information about the establishment of the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this was at the meeting of the council for security of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify the situation regarding the council for security of the municipality of Bosanski Samac. I am going to ask you now certain things, one thing at a time, and just give me yes or no answers, please. And my questions refer to who is on this council for security. The president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The president of the executive council?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The head of the public security station, the chief of police?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Territorial Defence headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The municipal secretary for all national defence?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In addition to them, the representatives of all the parties represented in the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean, then, that the municipal authorities, like all the political parties, the parliamentary parties in the territory of the municipality of Samac, were aware of the establishment of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody was informed about this, and some opposed its establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about the command of the 4th Detachment. Was it in the building of the Samac textile industry?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was either in Tekstilac or Mladost, one of those two factories. I think it was Mladost.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. As for the composition of the 4th Detachment, there were Serbs, Muslims, Croats, Montenegrins, Albanians, Bulgarians, in it? Briefly, members of all the ethnic groups that lived in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Predominantly it was Serbs, but there were also Muslims and Croats and Montenegrins for sure. I don't know whether there were any Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you mentioned the arming of the 4th Detachment. Was that also public?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was informed, at this meeting in Tekstilac, arms were distributed, or some members of the 4th Detachment took weapons in their cars to the homes of other members of the 4th Detachment. In other words, it was known that these weapons were being distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you something else. Can we agree that in the mass media, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group explained the role and the tasks of the JNA and the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you perhaps aware of the fact that he spoke on Radio Samac, on a certain programme?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you also say whether it was highlighted on all occasions that the reason for the existence of the 4th Detachment was to prevent interethnic conflicts, to prevent the northern boundary of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and to prevent the war from Croatia from spilling over to Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The commander was Radovan Antic, Reserve Captain First Class; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Jovo Savic, Reserve Captain First Class, was deputy commander for Radovan Andic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know Radovan and I know Simo. As for the rest, possibly may be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Simo Zaric was assistant commander for security, reporting morale and information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He was a Reserve Sergeant First Class; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Vukovic, Mehmed, was he also in the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to move on to another subject. It has to do with the situation in Bosanski Samac a few months before the conflict broke out. Can you confirm to me that in that period, a number of incidents occurred that caused anxiety among the citizens that made them feel insecure and frightened?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You already mentioned some of these things in your statement, some of these incidents. Now I'm going to ask you about some that were not mentioned. I'm just going to ask you to confirm whether they did occur or not. July 1991, the incident when the Croat army hit Pero Maksimovic from a rifle when he was in his boat on the river?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was a fast boat, wasn't it, a speed boat?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Also the incident when there was shooting on the Sava bridge, a certain Milos Miljic, and when he was wounded on that section of the bridge that belongs to Bosnia-Herzegovina, that this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Milos was wounded. I can't remember now how he was wounded, but yes, he was wounded, and I know that he was taken to hospital in Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel and witness, please pause after the two of you have spoken. You are using the same language, so you are forgetting that the interpreter -- in fact, the interpreter is one and the same person, interpreting the question and the answer, so please do pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you confirm for me that an incident occurred in which a small church was mined at the Orthodox cemetery in Bosanski Samac? According to my information, this was on the 27th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a church; it was a chapel. And I think that it was not demolished. I think there was lesser damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I asked whether it was mined.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a church; it was a small chapel. It had been mined, but it wasn't demolished altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that during 1991 and in the beginning of 1992, transmission lines in Samac and the surrounding area were mined several times?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such occasions. I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the kiosk [redacted] that was in the immediate vicinity of the police station had also been mined?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Also, finally, can you confirm that a slaughter took place on the 26th of March in the Serb village of Sijekovac that was carried out by the HVO and the ZNG of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That was in the municipality of Bosanski Brod.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know that there was warfare in Brod, but I don't know about the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I shall agree with the statement that you made, namely, that none of these cases has been solved. As for shedding more light on this, can you tell me whether at that time the chief of police in Bosanski Samac was Vinko Dragicevic, an ethnic Croat?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the same time, was the chief of the crime prevention service Dragan Lukac, also an ethnic Croat?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At that time, the investigating judges of the municipal court in Bosanski Samac, weren't they Seljic Zeljko and Stanic Zeljko -- Stanic Zdenko. Both were ethnic Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the prosecutor was a Serb, and you seem to be skipping things. Also, the commander of the police station was a Serb, the chief of the uniformed police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to go back to another event that you did not mention in your testimony here before the Tribunal, and that is the event that occurred on the 14th of February, 1992. It occurred at the Cafe Valentino. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean by the Dascara, this Valentino where the Dzakic house is?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, while playing with a bomb, a grenade, were two young men killed, Enver Bobic and Mersad Hadzialijagic, ethnic Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And also a young girl of Serb ethnicity was severely wounded?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These two young men that I mentioned, were they members of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Bobic's father was a member of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And what about the father of Hadzialijagic, that is to say, Hasan? Was he a member?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Hasan wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After this event there was unrest in town, was there not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And for the death of those two young men, Serbs of the JNA were accused of the crime. Was it like that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that kind of rumour was spread, that one of the Serbs had thrown a bomb or grenade into the cafe. But later on it turned out not to be true, but public opinion flared as a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in order to quieten tensions, a rally, citizens' rally, was held of the local community of Bosanski Samac and that it was held in the cinema hall, the kino hall?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And at the rally you yourself spoke, as well as Mr. Simo Zaric and some other citizens; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that took place on the 20th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly it could have been that date, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours could bear with me for one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before we move on to another area, I should just like to discuss one more incident. I have a few questions in that regard. I'm referring to the arrest of Simo Krunic and a certain man called Sveta Mitrovic. This was carried out by members of the Green Beret. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that they were disarmed on the bridge across the Sava River. Now, who disarmed them, I don't know. They were the other side of the Sava. Whether they were the Zengas, the Croatian National Guard Corps, and I know that Lukac and Izetbegovic went to fetch the weapons, to return them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. I should like now to move on to another topic, and that is the barricades. According to what you said, Alija Fitozovic engaged your men from the SDA patrol, and other citizens with arms, and they set up barricades at two entrances into town. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you something with respect to those two entrances at which the barricades had been erected. Were they entrances from the Serb villages of Pisari and Tisina?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were entrances from the directions of those two villages, but other villages as well. They were the only two roads leading into Samac. And the Croatian villages go through that, have to pass through that entrance too, people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we also agree that the barricades were not set up at the entrance from the direction of the Croatian village of Prud? Can we agree to that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the bridge across the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The members of the reserve police force manned those barricades as well? They were there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe they were there. I don't know actually. I didn't know about the barricades. But I don't think they were. But as I say, I can't say with certainty because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that it was because of those barricades in the neighbouring Croatian villages that their armed forces were placed on the alert?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, both in the Croatian and Serbian villages, both before and after the barricades, there were Serbian guards, Serb guards, and Croatian guards or watches. This is the only thing that the Muslims did. Now, when the Serb forces were in Crkvina would levy a toll that had to be paid, so it wasn't the result of those barricades, it wasn't because of the barricades that the village watches or village guards were set up in Croatian and Serb villages. So that was six months before. They had been set up six months before. And the Serb police force separated in the summer of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Sorry, I noticed you but I thought I should wait until the answer was complete. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I'm not objecting so far, but there is talk of armed forces and there seems to be something that's understood between the witness and the counsel, Defence counsel, but it's not apparent to me what these armed forces were, and the Chamber might be assisted to know what exactly they are talking about when they refer -- when both the witness and counsel refer to it. The question is: "Can we agree that it was because of these barricades in the neighbouring Croatian villages that their armed forces were placed on alert." I'm not sure if they are talking about Croatian villages in Bosanski Samac, across the border, and what are these armed forces anyway. So the Chamber might be assisted to know that, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly. Maybe counsel can clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard the comments made by my learned colleague of the Prosecution. Now, when I said "armed forces in Croatian villages," can you confirm that in the Croatian villages - I'm asking you about them now only, without wishing to imply anything - that there were organised forces with weapons, that is to say armed? MR. DI FAZIO: Again, I'm grateful to my learned friend, I think we are getting there, and I'm grateful for his clarification, but we just need to go a little further. I'm still not quite sure. Are we talking about in Bosanski Samac or across the river in Croatia? That's all I want to know. I think it's probably Bosanski Samac, but I'm just not certain, and I think we should be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think counsel can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am talking about the Croatian villages in the environs of Bosanski Samac, the Bosanski Samac municipality, in fact.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw those armed forces that you mention. I heard rumours that the people were arming themselves in the Croatian villages, but that I saw units or knew of their existence, I did not. Now, this reserve police force probably was carrying arms when they set up the barricades, and had the watch -- watches and so forth. I never saw a unit. I never saw five people carrying arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have a few more questions regarding the barricades. First, the individuals at the barricades, were they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were mostly Muslims, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From your testimony here before the Tribunal, I take it that they were armed?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Apart from Alija Fitozovic, whom you mentioned, were -- Ibrahim Salkic, nicknamed Ibela, at the barricades, was he there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly Ibela was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about a few others, if you can say whether they were or were not. Osman Mesic, nicknamed Semso?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Srna Safet?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I know for sure that Semso was there but this other one, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Srna Hakija?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fuad Jasenica?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May we agree that the police from the police station of Bosanski Samac did not undertake anything with respect to those barricades, did not do anything about them?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the barricades were set up, the chief of police from Sarajevo came and he was stationed at the unit on the bridge. He came and asked that they be disbanded. And then I became included in the dismantling of those barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What I meant was specifically whether any police action was taken to disband the barricades.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not police, but political. Political action was taken to disband the barricades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Can you explain the word "barricades"? What did it involve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at the entrance into town, a truck would be parked across the street, blocking traffic, and people could pass. But basically it was a roadblock with a truck, and that was the result of a JNA drive that night. And then these people went to these -- to set up the barricade, this roadblock. This was stupid. But the police in town had raised tensions. Tensions were high. And so the barricades were set up which shouldn't have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, with respect to the immediate event -- the event that took place immediately prior to the erection of the barricades, could we clarify one point? Arms were taken from SDA patrols, is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from the seizing of arms, they came to the Cafe Buco, they stopped there with their jeep, and there was a demonstration of force of some kind there. And in view of everything that had preceded, that had gone before, the mining and so on, tensions were so high that it was easy to rally people for this kind of endeavour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm interested in this seizure of arms from the SDA patrols.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons were in the vehicle belonging to the SDA. They didn't have it outside. The weapons were in the car. And somebody said, whether the people from the 4th Detachment or whoever, told the JNA patrol that these guys had some weapons, and they came there, came to that car, and confiscated the weapons that were in the trunk of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All I'm asking is whether the military police seized those weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, please pause. It's creating problems because the transcript won't be clear. Do remember to pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, with respect to this incident, I was interested in one particular point. Was it the military police who seized those weapons?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was informed that it was the military police, but it was the JNA, at all events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me now move on to another area which follows on from what we've just been discussing. In your statement before this Trial Chamber, you said that within the frameworks of the town of Samac, an agreement had been reached, according to which the 4th Detachment would patrol the embankment towards the rivers Sava and Bosna. Is that correct? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the 4th Detachment feared an attack from the Croatians from Croatia, then I think that from the Croatian Prud and perhaps others, they said that if you're afraid, then your patrols should be positioned along that embankment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm interested in that particular agreement. Was it reached at a meeting held in the local community?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the local community, a municipal facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you present?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the president of the local community council attend the meeting, Safet Hadzialijagic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that Safet was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to learn. Mr. Tihic, let's move on again to another area. Can you confirm the fact that between the SDA and HDZ in Samac, within the frameworks of Samac, that there was daily cooperation with respect to preparations for an armed conflict? Were they holding daily preparations?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't daily cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, I paraphrased something that you wrote down in your memoirs and has to do with what took place after the barricades. You said the following: "After that, we engaged in daily cooperation with the HDZ for defence preparations." That's what you stress.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that wasn't put in the best way, but especially between the SDA and HDZ, as two parties, this cooperation did not exist in defence preparations. There might have been between Alija Fitozovic and Marko Bozanovic, who were in the TO staff and headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't cooperate because of my position as president of the party, and I was opposed to cooperation just between two sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We'll come to that topic. On the 19th of March, 1992, you did attend the meeting in Prud, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived when the meeting was drawing to a close. I wasn't there from the start of the meeting, because I didn't like the idea of this meeting being held, but then I went to see what they were discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about some of the people who, according to my information, attended that meeting. Was a man called Stjepan Blazanovic there, nicknamed Blazo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was he there as the representative of the army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from Hasici or a village around there, and he came to instruct. And as far as I was able to understand, he had fought in Croatia. He had had some experience in fighting. But everything fell through. Nothing came of it. I said, "There's absolutely no way that any headquarters of that kind or staff could be formed," and Marko Bozanovic supported me. Because it was absurd that people from outside could come in and tell you about war. I wasn't about to accept any of that. I didn't want any kind of crisis staff to be set up jointly between Croats and Bosniaks. I said that the Serbs would have to be there too. I said that loud and clear, publicly, and nothing came of that meeting. And half of them were drunk anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something with respect to the major there. He was in the same capacity?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were some strange stories, rumours, going around.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The reason for the meeting, the purpose of the meeting, was to found a joint crisis staff. That was the idea of the meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the idea, but it didn't go through because I was opposed to that idea, and so were the Croats. Marko Bozanovic was opposed to the idea as well. And they couldn't wait for me to turn up to stand up in opposition against the other two, because they were a little afraid to stand up for themselves and present that view.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The proposal was made at the meeting that the president of this joint Crisis Staff should be Filip Evic, on behalf of the HDZ, and that you should be the vice-president of that Crisis Staff, the other side?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the proposal, but I didn't accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The proposals for commanders were put forward of that Crisis Staff, and those proposals were that they should be Marko Bozanovic, from the HDZ side, and Alija Fitozovic on the SDA side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I know that for the president and vice-president, that was true, but I don't know about this. Possibly. Possibly. I just can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, another meeting was held, if I can say, discussing the same subject, in the Croatian village of Grebnice; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that a meeting was held later on, but I didn't attend it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And was another representative of the SDA at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was probably Fitozovic, Alija Fitozovic. Later on I heard people were saying that he had been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, this brings me to my next question. Can you confirm the fact that you yourself and Izet Izetbegovic, on behalf of the SDA party, and Filip Evic and Mato Nujic, on behalf of the HDZ party, at your own initiative, sent a proposal to the Ministry of Defence, to Mr. Jerko Doko and the commander of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the effect that Marko Bozanovic should become commander of the TO staff in Bosanski Samac and Alija Fitozovic should become the Chief of Staff? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That proposal was sent by Mato Nujic, as president of the municipality, or mayor, but I took part in discussing that agreement, and the group, the team you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And was that on behalf of the HDZ party? That is included in the question: on behalf of the HDZ party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The proposal was sent by the president of the municipality on behalf of the SDS, HDZ, and SDA, all of them, as president of the Municipal Assembly, as the authorised person to propose the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, the proposal to appoint as municipal commander of the TO staff, the Chief of Staff -- now, is it the Municipal Assembly who is, by virtue of its authority, in charge of putting forward the proposal?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about the Municipal Assembly, but it is the duty of the president of the municipality, or mayor, to oversee something like that and confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With respect to this proposal, was a meeting held of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were the representatives of the other parliamentary parties in the Municipal Assembly consulted?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to ask Mato Nujic that. I don't know. He consulted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this procedure was contrary to the regulations that were in force at the time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm or refute it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like the evidence P13 and P13 ter to be shown to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- the witness, yes. B/C/S version to be given to the witness and English version to the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, this exhibit has already been shown to you while you were examined by the Prosecution; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I looked carefully at the transcript. You said that the list included 100 people. That's what it said in the transcript. Now, for purposes of clarification, could you please take a look at the list once again?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list? This is just a letter. I don't see a list. What list?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, the document was in two parts and there was an attachment to it which was a list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm wondering. Was there? It was produced by the Prosecutor. MR. DI FAZIO: Just off the top of my head, I can't assist the Chamber. I'm asking my case manager to have a look and see if we can locate our copy, but I can't answer that query just at the moment, if Your Honours please. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Do the Defence have a copy? We don't seem to -- because a list was discussed in the letter, as it is clearly shown. Does the Defence have the list? Was that -- was that numbered or did it just have one number? Does the registry assistant have it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, only the letter was submitted, according to our list. No attachment or list was submitted with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher show the list to the Prosecutor? MR. DI FAZIO: This certainly looks very familiar to me, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because if it's not with the registry assistant, maybe it wasn't attached, because it should have been inside the same plastic. MR. DI FAZIO: One would think so, if the letter and list was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe searching the transcript to see whether or not -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I wonder if the Court could assist by telling us how the exhibit is described, if there is an exhibit list how it is described, as letter and list or simply as letter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No. It is described as letter addressed by the Party of Democratic Action to city command attention for the municipal headquarter, dated 13 April, 1992. MR. DI FAZIO: Surprising that the list isn't mentioned either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio -- [no microphone] MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that might account for the absence of the list. On the other hand, the letter also says a copy of the list is enclosed so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [No microphone]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are sorry, your microphone is not on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, I was referring to the fourth paragraph: "At your request, we shall deliver the list of individuals." So the query I'm putting is, well, was it enclosed with this? Because it could possibly have been awaiting the request. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that might account for an absence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If the description of the exhibit is just a letter, then it wasn't produced. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Does my learned friend have -- could he quickly direct us to the portion in the transcript where Mr. Tihic -- where it was produced to Mr. Tihic, if he has his notes? If he has the notes, we can quickly go back to the transcript and have a look at that, and that might give us a clue as to whether it was more than just a letter that was tendered at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Maybe I can assist. The letter was submitted and admitted on the 17th of September this year. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So it would be the transcript of the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I could assist my learned colleague. It's on page 1356. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'm grateful to my learned friend. That's of considerable assistance. As I read the transcript from that day, it looks pretty clear to me that there was no list -- yes, yes. I've found it. Page 1356, question: "The document refers to a list in the first paragraph. What list was that, do you think? Because obviously it's not attached to this document." So that explains it. There never was a list and it's not part of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So this exhibit is just a letter. But counsel -- if counsel has a list which he thinks pertains to this letter, then he can have it shown to the witness and deal with it in the way he thinks he wants to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Perhaps you may want to ask the witness if he can remember if a request was received and if a list was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, you have heard the suggestions of the Trial Chamber and the suggestion of the Honourable Judge Singh. Did you attach a list?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether a list was given, but our aim was to have all armed persons and all weapons sent to the Territorial Defence. And Alija Fitozovic was doing this, so he's probably the one who had the list. So all of those who had weapons through the SDA, or with the assistance of the SDA, were supposed to report to the Territorial Defence headquarters. I assume that there was a list. I cannot claim that a list came with this letter but Alija Fitozovic would be in a better position to say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, since now I don't have enough copies of this list, the copy that I have given to the usher, if this could be just shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe it can be -- maybe we can have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: First he can look at it, because he has to look at it at close range and then we can have it on the ELMO before you ask questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It could not have been a list this long, that's for sure, because there weren't that many weapons. This is a list of organised citizens who are putting themselves at the disposal of the TO headquarters. You see they were putting themselves to the disposal -- at the disposal of the TO to go into units, but this was not a list of those who had weapons. There weren't that many weapons. I remember that the TO headquarters were supposed to get a list of those who wished to join the Territorial Defence and this is probably that list. The list of those who want to join the TO staff. As I said, it could have been about 100 rifles and the rest at the most, the 50 that came from Dzakovo, 20 from Senaid Memic, and 30 -- 30 of Senaid Memic and also when that truck had broke down. So it could have had 100 -- there could have been 100 on this list at the maximum, and here it is 220.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have it numbered for identification purposes only, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ter, I think? Is it not in Serbo-Croat? The list is in Serbo-Croat, I mean the title? Is it in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D14/4 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There really are people here who have nothing to do with weapons or any such thing, no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, if I have understood this correctly, what you have been saying, namely, these are people who had put themselves at the disposal of the TO?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Territorial Defence headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then you said that perhaps there could have been about 100 of those who had weapons, these illegal weapons, to term them that way?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is quite clear from what I have stated to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that people also had legal weapons, carbines, pistols, other kinds of weapons, that were permitted, so to speak, according to existing regulations?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, there were hunters who had hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. That is the only thing I wish to ask you in this connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender the original of this document that we have, and to have a number for it, not as identification number but the evidence number, because we are going to use this document in the future, during the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What do you want to tender it as? Because the witness has said that list you have shown him, which has just been given an ID, D14/4 ter ID, is a list of people who were volunteering to join the TO, not a list discussed in P13 ter. I hope you understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I ask the Prosecution? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm not sure what document my learned friend is referring to. Is that the original of the document the witness now has before him? May I ask that? So it's exactly the same as the photocopy that was produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher can collect the document and show both what is described as original and the copy to the Prosecution so that they can be sure what the document is. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you answer, is there anything on that document which is in Serbo-Croat which -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- you don't -- MR. DI FAZIO: The title, there are what I assume are nicknames, and some street numbers, and there are other words that might be comments or might be street names. I can't tell. But certainly there's a heading that will have to be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The translation will come. But for purposes of your re-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: No. For purposes of my re-examination, I'm not objecting to its provision in this form without a full translation at this stage. It's only the title, and I can easily find out what that means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it can be admitted into evidence? MR. DI FAZIO: No. I'd ask that it would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps not now. MR. DI FAZIO: Not now, no. I mean, there's not much of a foundation for the document at this stage. I'd ask that it be marked for identification. And we've also heard from the witness that Alija Fitozovic is the man who probably could tell the Chamber more about this document than this particular witness. So I would ask that it simply be marked for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But you're satisfied that this is an original? MR. DI FAZIO: It appears to me, if Your Honours please, to be an original. It appears to me to be typed directly onto paper, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall simply mark it for identification. If you still wish to have it produced in evidence, you have understood the points the Prosecution have raised. MR. DI FAZIO: It may be, if Your Honours please, that after I've had time to ascertain what I can about the history of this document, because I think I've seen it before, the Prosecution may have information about it that I don't have at any fingertips right now. That being the case, I may withdraw my objection to it going -- to it being fully admitted into evidence at a later point, but at this stage I would ask simply that it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said, that it will be marked for identification. If, at a later stage, you find out whatever you have to find out and you are satisfied that it's okay, then you will raise it. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I will. Thank you. And can I ask, of course, that the exhibit number be given to the original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The copy and the original. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, have you seen this document before during the course of your work in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, I would like to move on to another subject now. These are the events in the night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992. In your statement before this Tribunal, you said that around 2.00 in the morning you heard gunshots, that you looked through the window and saw some members of the 4th Detachment moving behind houses and trees with rifles and that you recognised some of them. You also stated that some were in uniform and others were in civilian clothes, and that they were moving in the direction of the Bosna River. Is that correct, that that is what you stated?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to put a few questions to you in connection with these words of yours. This was going on during the night, right, around 2.30, 3.00 a.m.? That's the month of April. It's still dark during the night, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, that day was a cloudy day. As a matter of fact, at one point there was even a bit of snow.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You already said that these people were hiding between the houses and the trees as they were moving along; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since my yard is wide and big, they were behind trees and things like that. Some were crawling, others were hiding behind trees. But I had a big light bulb outside, and that illuminated the yard very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They were moving, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some were standing a bit, others were moving. And then also, towards the bank of the Bosna River --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about something. You said that you recognised some of them. Can you tell me who were the people you recognised? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By sight I remember some of these people. I remember this salesperson from the furniture place. I can't remember his name. And then also a neighbour's son. I recognised him. Jelisije -- I can't remember all these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you something in this connection. Mr. Tihic, you never saw an official list of the members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You did not. Also, you never saw the 4th Detachment lined up in full?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, during the further proceedings, during your testimony, you mentioned Mico Pavlovic, that you were at his home.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was also a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You found him at home on the telephone and then you went home; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Most of the Serbs in town were in the 4th Detachment, and also part of the Muslims, and thereby I assumed that they were members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, I read your recollections carefully, and at one point you said that in the attack on Samac, the following took part: Arkan's units, the Serb militia, the Serb TO, and finally, the JNA. Can you perhaps tell me: These people that you saw, were they perhaps the Serb TO?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were people from town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you also mentioned Safet Hadzialijagic, nicknamed Pop, president of the council of the local commune, and that he came to see you and proposed that you invite the JNA and the 4th Detachment --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He phoned me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise -- so that you would create a buffer zone between you and the paramilitary formations. That was his idea. Was that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because people were saying that the paramilitaries in Gornja Mahala were killing people, and he called me and said, "Well, look, let's put the JNA in between." In between who? [Realtime transcript read in error: Q. In between who?]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something else about the 4th Detachment now. You will answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The answer wasn't given. The witness said he received this call from somebody who said, "Well, let's put the JNA in between." Then the counsel asked, "In between who?" And then you say -- then you continue talking before the witness answered.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that the witness said, "In between who?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because it's recorded as a question, so ... Yes. So the transcript should be -- so it is the witness who asked, "In between who?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe when I posed this question that I was talking about Hadzialijagic, Safet, with the nickname Pop, and that was, by my view, completely clear to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you something related to collecting weapons from citizens on the part of the 4th Detachment. Did they do that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after the attack on Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, afterwards.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was in an apartment, and as far as I can remember, there were the members of the JNA who were there. And I saw Salkic, Ibrahim, [redacted]. And now, with them, whether there were those from the 4th Detachment, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not going to insist. I just asked you if you knew.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the members of the 4th Detachment took the right banks of the Sava and Bosna rivers, respectively, in order to prevent the HVO from penetrating?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, and the bridge on the Drina [as interpreted] -- on the Bosna.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter stands corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. Now I would like to move on to other subjects. After taking a statement from you, after hearing your statement, can we say that Simo Zaric made quite an effort to find a way of having you released?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to move on to the subject of your transfer to the military barracks in Brcko. Would it be fair to say that it was precisely Simo Zaric, the person who initiated your transfer, as well as of others, from the Territorial Defence in Samac to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know he talked on the phone in front of me, and he said to this Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic - I think he was talking to him - "If they stay a few days longer, they will all get killed, so take them, transfer them," something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we say that he was sincerely pleased that things were organised in that way? You said that he hugged you, kissed you.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to your own statement, nobody beat you at Brcko.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only a little bit while we were being frisked. Well, we can say that nobody beat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Some of the prisoners also got medical assistance; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The food was better too, and more generous?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The army treated you considerably better?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You could even go out into the compound of the barracks, to put it that way?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were allowed to clean it, sweep it. Those who wanted to clean it and sweep it managed to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that you and the other prisoners were transferred from the Territorial Defence in Samac to the military barracks in Brcko, and that eliminated the danger of you being killed or beaten up by the paramilitaries or the police?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was considerably different there, quite different there. In Samac, anybody could just come and kill you and mistreat you. Over here, there was some kind of order after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, now I would like to move on to that day when -- oh, I'm sorry. When you were brought to the military barracks in Brcko, did Simo Zaric escort you to Brcko? If you know that, say so, and if you don't know, just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he did. I did not see him. Perhaps he was in another vehicle, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to move on to that day when, from the military barracks in Brcko, you were returned, so to speak, to Bosanski Samac for a brief period of time in order to give a statement for TV Novi Sad. If I understood you correctly, you were asked by the prison warden - this was a bald captain with plaster on his arm - and he said that you should go to Bosanski Samac and give a statement for the TV?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then they put you into a Pinzgauer, a military vehicle, and then they drove you away?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was Simo Zaric with you then during that transfer?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, it's 1.00 by our clock in the courtroom. Today, the afternoon session will start at 1430 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, and how long shall we have, as you mentioned yesterday, this afternoon, to have a break after one and a half hours and then another half an hour -- another one and a half hours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When we start at 1430, we shall sit up to 1615 hours, one and a half hours. We shall have a break at 1615. No, not at 1615. We shall have a break at 1600 hours to 1615, a 15 minutes break, and then continue up to 1715, just for one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it will be one and a half hours, a short break, and then one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We're continuing with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We're not having -- we're not receiving translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, I took advantage of the lunch break to look through the transcript from the trial, and I have a question to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have interpretation now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, you said that all the Serbs from Bosanski Samac were in the 4th Detachment; is that right? I'm just quoting that section.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And during your testimony, you also mentioned the Serbian Territorial Defence when you talked about the occupation of Samac.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that certain ethnic Serbs from Bosanski Samac were also members of that so-called Serb Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were only in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I should like now to move to another topic, and that is a television programme by TV Novi Sad. You saw an excerpt here, and I would like to ask you if you recall that footage. Is it correct that at the beginning of that programme, Stevan Nikolic spoke?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes. Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you were in Samac, when you were brought from Brcko, did you see him there in the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That man, Stevan Nikolic, who was a lieutenant colonel, he was the commander of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA. That's him, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was he the superior officer to Mr. Simo Zaric by the chain of command and military hierarchy? Do you happen to know the fact that the participation of Mr. Zaric in the programme was following his orders?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm just not clear what the answer is. Is the answer an answer to the first question or the second question? That's the way the transcript appears on my screen. I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There are two questions, yes, so maybe the counsel can clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have the problem of the transcript here. There were two questions. I asked you first whether the lieutenant colonel was the superior officer - and I think you said yes -

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- to Simo Zaric. And your answer was yes?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you said you didn't know as far as the second question was concerned; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, when you were transferred from the barracks in Brcko back to Samac, were you frightened?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived, was Simo Zaric already in the SUP offices?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was. I know that Vlado Sarkijan and Kruno Sifo met me, and I think he was somewhere too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that occasion, did you ask Simo Zaric to be close by, next to you, for your own safety and security?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember. Possibly, but I can't remember. I know that Vlado and the others hurried things up to get it over with as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That brings me to my next question, yes. I wanted to ask you the following: All of you who were there, did Simo Zaric hurry you up? Was he hurrying you up because there was the possibility of these Sareni turning up again, as they were termed?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I have one more question with respect to that event. So right before -- the interview was conducted by a TV Novi Sad journalist?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He talked to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move on to a different area? And that is your transfer from the barracks in Brcko to the barracks in Bijeljina. You have already stated that the captain who was in charge called Mr. Lukac and yourself and told you, more or less, that the war had broken out in Brcko and that that was the reason why they were transferring you to Bijeljina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May we then take it that the transfer from Brcko to Bijeljina was motivated for your own safety -- was for the purposes of your own safety and security?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we now go back to the 26th of April? That was the day when you were transferred from Bosanski Samac to Brcko. In your statement, you said that on that particular day, Stevan Todorovic told you something along the lines of, well, he's giving you another chance. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan came to where I was and he sort of said, "I'm going to give you another chance. You're going to go with these others to Brcko." Because I had the feeling that the ones who stayed behind would be killed. That was my feeling. That was what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with respect to the actual words that were uttered --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he said more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could he have said that on the 29th of April, when you gave the interview, those words? Might they have been spoken then?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were spoken prior to my transfer to Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. I'd like now to move on and ask you some questions related to the personality of Mr. Zaric, what he was like. May we agree that Simo Zaric was a respected man in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mostly, although there were people that did not respect him, but mostly he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that that was the prevailing opinion about him?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He was active in the Kombinat Sports Club, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I really don't remember. I know that he was politically involved, that he was a hunter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you whether you happened to know anything about his membership in the cultural and arts society from the Croatian village of Prud. He took part in folklore?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember he did take part in folklore meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That was in the village of Prud, was it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if that is in the village of Prud but I do know that he attended and took part in these folklore performances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: His wife is a Muslim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that his daughter is married to a Croat?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One of his sisters is married to a Croat and the other is married to a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May we then agree that Simo Zaric was truly a Yugoslav by affiliation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And finally, was Simo ever a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the time I knew him, he was not. I don't think he was after that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tihic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a second just to prepare?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Tihic. I am attorney Pantelic, Defence counsel for Mr. Blagoje Simic. Let me start off by saying on -- in my own name, and I think in the name of all my colleagues and our clients, that is to say I would like to congratulate you for your appointment as president of the SDA party for Bosnia-Herzegovina, although I did congratulate you on Monday when we saw each other in passing.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you were in The Hague the last time, you were the vice-president and now you are the president, so The Hague seems to be lucky for you.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, preparations for the congress were already underway, so Hague didn't actually influence that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I didn't mean in that sense. I just meant that it was a happy coincidence.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, too. Mr. Tihic, I would like us to clarify a few points of your testimony. They are technical matters, nothing much, but as we do have a transcript, we want to have a clear one. I have your witness statement, the one you gave between the 22nd and 23rd of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
